name: animal-borne tags behavior benchmark
description: Animal-borne sensors (`bio-loggers') can record a suite of kinematic and environmental data, which are used to elucidate animal ecophysiology and improve conservation efforts. Machine learning techniques are used for interpreting the large amounts of data recorded by bio-loggers, but there exists no common framework for comparing the different machine learning techniques in this domain. This makes it difficult to, for example, identify patterns in what works well for machine learning-based analysis of bio-logger data. It also makes it difficult to evaluate the effectiveness of novel methods developed by the machine learning community. To address this, we present the Bio-logger Ethogram Benchmark (BEBE), a collection of datasets with behavioral annotations, as well as a modeling task and evaluation metrics. reputation: A recent, widely cited benchmark for animal-borne sensor behavior recognition, valued for its taxonomic diversity and public availability.
notes: Non-LLM, multimodal time-series benchmark; performance varies substantially by species and behavior class, and class imbalance can be significant.
